title: Finishing Pages, step 3 — where the page's chat sits

steps.path: An open page → the chat button beside the gear, next to the page's name
steps.headline: On a computer, where should a page's chat sit?
steps.notice: The chat is your normal chat, just narrower, the same way the buddy shows it. The button beside the page's settings gear opens and closes it. The conversation is a sample about the Money page.
steps.risk: Mockup: the chat shows a sample conversation. New chat and which conversation each page keeps come with the build.

variants.label: Chat on the left
variants.summary: The chat takes the page list's place, and the page keeps its full width. The list comes back when you close the chat. This is closest to what you described: chat on one side, page on the other.

variants.label: Chat on the right
variants.summary: The page list stays and the chat opens on the right, like Files beside a chat. You can switch pages without closing the chat.
variants.risk: The page is squeezed between the two: look at how the Needs you cards wrap.

variants.label: Chat floating over
variants.summary: The page keeps everything, and the chat is a card over its bottom right corner. Good for quick questions.
variants.risk: It covers part of the page, so a change it makes there can be hidden under it.

steps.path: A page on your phone → the chat button
steps.headline: On a phone, the chat rises as a sheet over the bottom of the page, leaving the top of the page visible.
steps.changed: A phone has no room beside the page, so the chat slides up over it, with the same title row (New chat, close) and message box.
steps.notice: You still see the top of the page, so a change the chat makes up there shows while you talk.
